project.title: Beilinson–Bloch Heights and the Strong Zero-Curvature Green Conjecture
project.subtitle: Actual Green forms, canonical pairings, and arithmetic finiteness
project.summary: The principal-push theorem constructs full Beilinson–Bloch height pairings from Strong Green under stated analytic foundations. General Strong Green existence, positivity and arithmetic finiteness guide the remaining research.
project.motivation:
Heights measure the arithmetic size of geometric objects. On curves, degree-zero divisors lead to the Néron–Tate pairing on the Jacobian. In higher codimension, the corresponding pairing should connect algebraic cycles, local intersection theory, and arithmetic finiteness.

The principal-push theorem (PH16; Theorem 7.5) proves that Strong G at every finite completion in both complementary codimensions gives the canonical real pairing on the full geometrically homologically trivial rational Chow groups, within the stated analytic foundations. Its proof handles reciprocity, finite summation and rational-equivalence descent. The central general existence problem is to construct the required actual Green forms; positivity, nondegeneracy and arithmetic finiteness are subsequent questions.

The local target is an actual Mihatsch \(\delta\)-form, not only a current. The arithmetic target counts images of integral cycles in rational Chow groups or their quotients. These choices determine the constructions and the obstructions studied here.
project.programme: The construction strand studies actual finite traces, support-preserving Green forms, numerical model certificates, and the image of the original Chow group in residual period spaces. The properties strand separates curve-visible abelian contributions from a residual Griffiths quotient. Arithmetic regulators, integral lattices, and fields of definition then provide distinct approaches to Northcott finiteness. A comparison strand connects normalized determinant metrics, local heights, and degeneration in families.
